name: Livestreamed rhinoplasty

card.summary: Nose surgery broadcast live to an audience, used by looksmaxxing creators to reshape the nose and document the change in real time.
card.note: Surgery under anaesthesia carries standard operative risks; broadcasting it has drawn ethical debate.

quick.overview:
Rhinoplasty reshapes the nose, for example by changing its size, nostrils or profile, and it can change how the whole face looks in profile and from the front. A livestreamed rhinoplasty is the same operation with part of it, and the lead-up, broadcast live to viewers.

The best-known looksmaxxing example reported in news coverage is influencer Clavicular, who streamed his June 2026 procedure with surgeon Michael Salzhauer. The surgery itself is an established procedure with a long clinical literature; the livestream format is new and the debate around it is mostly about ethics.
quick.how: The operation is performed by a surgeon, either through incisions inside the nose (closed) or with a small incision across the columella (open), with bone and cartilage reshaped and a splint applied. In a livestream, the creator announces the plan, streams around the procedure, and later shares recovery and results updates.
quick.risks: Swelling can take a year or more to settle fully, and revision surgery is needed in roughly 5 to 20 percent of rhinoplasties according to Wikipedia. Listed deformities include pollybeak, saddle nose and open roof deformity. Critics of live broadcasting raise concerns about patient privacy, distraction in the operating room and pressure on young viewers.

lead: A livestreamed rhinoplasty is a nose operation broadcast live over a streaming platform. Rhinoplasty is plastic surgery that changes the shape, size or proportions of the nose, and it can be cosmetic, functional or reconstructive.[1]

Looksmaxxing creators treat nose surgery as part of hardmaxxing, the community's term for surgical change, and some publicise it to their audiences. In early June 2026, news outlets reported that influencer Clavicular (Braden Peters, 20) livestreamed his rhinoplasty on the platform Kick, with surgeon Michael Salzhauer, known online as Dr. Miami; the stream drew thousands of viewers.[2]
The stream renewed debate about the ethics of broadcasting medical procedures, particularly those involving young influencers with large audiences.[2]

chain: Surgeon reshapes nasal bone, cartilage or nostrils
Facial balance and the creator's appearance change, shown to followers
angle.text: The surgery itself changes the nose; the livestream adds a public record of the plan, the day and the healing. Creators use the stream to show their audience the process and the result.

paras: In rhinoplasty the surgeon separates skin from the nasal framework, reshapes bone and cartilage, closes the incisions and applies a splint or stent.[1] Closed rhinoplasty keeps all incisions inside the nose, while open rhinoplasty adds a small incision across the columella for better visibility; Wikipedia reports no significant long-term outcome difference between them.[1] Cartilage grafts may come from the septum, ear or rib.[1]

Rhinoplasty is already prominent on social platforms: a #NoseJobCheck trend on TikTok in early 2021 featured before-and-after videos, with the audio used in over 120,000 videos and the hashtag passing a billion views.[1]

Reports dated June 3, 2026 say Clavicular broadcast the procedure in real time on Kick, including before and during the operation, and that planned changes to the nostrils were described as subtle.[2] Kick-focused accounts called it the first streamed rhinoplasty, a claim the coverage did not verify.[2] One commentator suggested he might pursue more extensive surgery such as double jaw surgery to sustain viewership; the report notes this was speculation.[2]

Recovery involves swelling that can take a year or more to resolve fully, and smoking can impair healing.[1] Revision surgery is needed in roughly 5-20% of rhinoplasties.[1] Ethical concerns raised in coverage focus on broadcasting a medical procedure to a young audience.[2]

timeline.event: #NoseJobCheck trend popularises rhinoplasty before-and-after videos on TikTok.[1]
Clavicular livestreams his rhinoplasty on Kick.[2]
